### Investment Memo: ALNY — November 20, 2026

**Verdict**: BUY — staged initiation only | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $215 (+43% from $150.57) | Bull $321 / Bear $84
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**
Alnylam is the dominant RNAi platform whose stock has de-rated 69% on two guidance cuts and ATTR-CM share loss to BridgeBio's Attruby — a de-rating that now prices a franchise peak contradicted by a net-cash balance sheet, clean accounting, a $1B buyback, and open-market insider buying at the lows. At 2.9x 2027E sales and ~18.5x 2027E EPS, the market assigns roughly zero value to everything beyond Amvuttra. The catch is timing: leading indicators point to a Q4 revenue miss, and the Feb 11, 2027 print (Q4 + 2027 guidance + two readouts, deliberately stacked) is a negatively-skewed binary — so we initiate small and earn the right to size up.

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Macro UNFAVOURABLE on valuation (real 10Y ~2.4%, 30Y 5.47%, ~3 hikes priced; ALNY is the longest-duration name in the peer set) — but it is a ~25% amplifier, not the cause; credit is easy and XBI is rallying while ALNY falls. Sector NEUTRAL: RNAi flipped from orphan oligopoly to cardiology share-warfare; multiples compress faster than revenue grows.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM. Geopolitics genuinely favourable (US-anchored manufacturing = tariff-advantaged). Risk is domestic: MFN/TrumpRx status unconfirmed, IRA negotiation, 340B reform; securities class action filed; two FDA OPDP untitled letters on Amvuttra survival claims; vutrisiran patent-challenge-eligible since Jun 2026 — an underappreciated tail.
- **Value**: Narrow, *narrowing* moat; quality 7/10. Net cash ~$1.6–2.3B; EV/FY26E EBITDA ~13.7x, EV/FCF ~30x. Gross margin down ~9pts YoY; SBC ~6–9% of revenue. High-quality platform in a politically-priced end market — not a See's Candies.
- **Growth**: BUY. 2.0x 2030E consensus revenue = market pricing zero growth post-2026; Rule of 40 = 78. But hypergrowth is over (+65% → +18% → +15%) and the Q3 "beat" was a $1.87B deferred-tax artifact — underlying EPS ~$1.50 *missed*.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **NO REPORT — gap.** Quant agent returned empty; no systematic factor input.
- **Financial Risk**: MODERATE, deteriorating. Net cash, but ~$1.3B of out-of-the-money converts cash-settle 2027–28; SBC-adjusted FCF only ~$117M (~0.6% yield); a −20% revenue shock swings EBIT −$1.4B. Unresolved anomaly: $365M TTM interest on $1.28B of 0–1% converts implies undisclosed royalty-type obligations.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH. 33:1 insider sell/buy ratio ($18M sold at $300–333 *before* both cuts); CCO departed six days after the miss; class action; 79–89% single-franchise concentration; aging board. Counter-signal: Chair Schulman and Director Sigal bought ~$540K at $152–157.
- **ESG**: AVERAGE, modest drag. Pricing legitimacy (~$476k/yr vs ICER threshold; probable 7-year IRA clock) is an earnings risk, not an abstraction; governance 5/10 — good machinery, deteriorating behaviour. Clean environmental/safety record.
- **Alternative Data**: BEARISH near-term. "Amvuttra" search interest −24% off spring peak; Q4 tracking $1.35–1.42B vs $1.52B consensus (−4% to −7% miss); hiring at maintenance levels; litigation alerts multiplying; retail complacently bullish at lows.
- **Short / Contrarian**: NO EDGE. Explicitly no fraud (negative accruals four years, 1.67x cash conversion, $0 goodwill); the ~9x trailing P/E and Altman Z "distress" are artifacts and rejected. Bear case is public and priced; at $150 the $84/$321 distribution no longer pays a fresh short.

**Bull Case**
- **Asymmetric valuation**: 2.9x 2027E sales / 18.5x 2027E EPS for an 80%-gross-margin, GAAP-profitable platform with a 49.8% five-year CAGR; median sell-side PT ~$273 (+82%); quantified bull case $321 (+113%).
- **Balance sheet + alignment**: ~$2B net cash, $1B buyback (~5% of shares), board members writing personal checks at 12-month lows; zero goodwill; forensic review found no accounting manipulation.
- **Unpriced pipeline and cleared field**: Wainua failed in ATTR-CM; tafamidis generics pushed to 2031; zilebesiran ($30B+ hypertension TAM), nucresiran, CNS assets and the cemdisiran royalty stream are valued at ~zero. A Q1-2027 Fed pivot alone is worth +40–60% on duration mechanics.

**Bear Case**
- **Demand and credibility are broken**: two guidance cuts, two −25%+ single-day gaps, a filed class action, a departed CCO — and leading indicators (search, hiring, payer restrictions) point to another Q4 miss on Feb 11.
- **Margin structure is deteriorating, not dipping**: product gross margin 72% (from ~87% six quarters ago) on royalty stacking and GTN/340B pressure; SBC-adjusted FCF yield ~0.6%; FY25 sustainable net margin closer to 5% than headline.
- **One franchise, three attackers, hostile policy**: ~79–89% of revenue is TTR; Attruby is targeting 30–40% share with Pfizer entrenched; a ~$476k drug sits in the IRA/MFN/340B crosshairs with the patent-challenge window open since June 2026.

**Key Risks** (thesis-invalidation triggers; exit on any two)
1. Q4'26 Amvuttra < $1.10B sequentially **and** 2027 TTR guidance < ~$4.5B.
2. Product gross margin < 70% for two consecutive quarters (breaks platform leverage).
3. Attruby > 40% of new ATTR-CM starts.
4. OPDP escalation to warning letter / DOJ inquiry, or a credible ANDA/IPR filing against vutrisiran.
5. Convert wall (~$1.3B) cash-settled while revenue stalls → net cash flips to net debt inside 24 months.
6. Failure to backfill CCO by Q1'27 or further commercial-leadership churn.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
INITIATE **1.5%** in two 0.75% tranches at $148–156 (anchored to the insider prints); hard cap **3.0%**. Add +1.0–1.5% **only after Feb 11 confirmation** (Amvuttra ≥ $1.10B and 2027 TTR guide ≥ high-teens %). Price-review trigger $118 — a review level, not a resting stop at 50% vol. Sizing rationale: 49.8% annualised vol and **R² of 0.077 vs XBI (92% idiosyncratic variance)** make this a single-asset venture bet, not sector exposure; 3% would consume ~15% of a 10–12% portfolio risk budget. Event-driven mandates may substitute 0.75% equity + a Feb/Mar put spread. Optional pair: long ALNY / short BBIO (0.19 correlation) to isolate the ATTR-CM share shift.

**Dissent, gaps and challenges flagged**
- **Growth vs Alt Data resolved**: one is a 3-year valuation statement, the other an 11-week timing call; leading indicators win on timing — hence staged entry, not full size.
- **Rejected as evidence**: Altman Z "distress" (−0.02) and ~9x trailing P/E — both artifacts of the accumulated deficit and the $1.87B DTA release.
- **Unresolved before sizing above 1.5%**: net cash discrepancy ($1.63B vs $2.3B) and the interest-expense/royalty-obligation anomaly — pull the debt footnote. Also missing: Quant report, Q3'26 cash balance, MFN participation status, Value agent's final verdict (report truncated).

**Bottom line**: The bear case is real but priced; the platform, balance sheet, and insider buying are not. Buy small now, let Feb 11 decide whether this becomes a position or a lesson.

# ALNY — Portfolio Construction Recommendation
**Alnylam Pharmaceuticals | Healthcare / Biotechnology (RNAi) | Price $150.57 · Mkt cap ~$20.2B**
*Synthesis across 11 specialist reports (Quant Analyst report received **empty** — see data gaps)*

**Verified risk data (my own tools, reconciling conflicting agent claims):** 2-yr annualised vol **49.8%**, beta vs XBI **0.50**, **R² = 0.077** vs XBI, max drawdown **−69.9%**, alpha vs XBI (2y annualised) **−55.8%**. Correlation: SPY **0.14**, XBI **0.27**, IBB **0.34**, BBIO **0.19**, VRTX **0.20**.

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|

| **Macro Researcher** | **UNFAVOURABLE** (valuation axis) | Medium | Real 10Y ~2.4%, 30Y 5.47%, ~3 more hikes priced. ALNY is the **longest-duration name in the peer set** — but macro is a ~25% amplifier, not the cause. A Q1-27 Fed pivot = +40–60% on duration alone |
| **ESG Analyst** | AVERAGE / modestly negative | Medium | ~$476k/yr list price vs ICER threshold → payer + IRA risk is an *earnings* risk; governance **5/10** (good machinery, deteriorating behaviour); $1B buyback "is the tell" |
| **Quant Analyst** | **NO REPORT RECEIVED** | — | Output empty. Gap. |
| *Corroborating (sell-side)* | 10 of 12 PTs cut; **median ~$273.5**, range $225–350 | — | +82% to median PT; Stifel the sole Hold at $225 |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **HIGH agreement on facts / SPLIT on action**

**High consensus (11/11 agents, near-zero dissent) on the FACT PATTERN:**
1. The **science and platform are not the problem** — 7 approvals, clean accounting, $0 goodwill, best-in-class balance sheet, no fraud (Short Analyst looked and explicitly found none).
2. **Commercial conversion is deteriorating** and guidance credibility is impaired — two cuts, two −25%+ single-day gaps, CCO gone.
3. **Concentration is extreme** — 79–87% of revenue in one molecule, in the one indication attracting two well-capitalised rivals.
4. **The stock is cheap on normalized numbers** (median PT +82%; Short Analyst's bull case +113%) *because* of #2 and #3 — not by mistake.

**The genuine split — and how I resolve it:** Growth says BUY now; Alt Data says the Feb 11 print has a 4–7% revenue miss embedded. **These are not contradictory.** One is a 3-year statement, the other an 11-week timing call. The synthesis: the long-run risk/reward is favourable, but the **single largest near-term catalyst is skewed negative and is deliberately unresolvable in advance**. That argues for a real but small position now, with size withheld until Feb 11.

**Where I overrule an agent:** Growth argues the market is "pricing a franchise peak that the data does not support." Alt Data — the only agent with *leading* indicators — shows brand search interest decaying *faster* than reported demand. Leading beats coincident. I therefore discount Growth's urgency (not its valuation work) and treat Feb 11 as a near-term negative skew. Conversely, I overrule any bearish read from the **Altman Z-score (−0.02, "Distress")** and the **~9x trailing P/E**: both are artifacts (accumulated deficit; $1.87B one-time DTA release). The Short Analyst's rejection of both is correct and I adopt it.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.5% of portfolio now; hard cap 3.0%**

**Rationale — three independent sizing methods converge on "small":**

- **Volatility risk budget.** At **49.8% annualised vol**, a 1.5% position contributes ~75bp of portfolio vol; 3.0% contributes ~150bp. Against a 10–12% portfolio vol target, **3% already consumes 13–15% of the entire risk budget in one name.** That is the binding cap.
- **Diversification reality (the decisive number).** **R² vs XBI = 0.077** — **92% of ALNY's variance is idiosyncratic.** You get almost *no* biotech factor beta, only standalone binary event risk. Correlation to SPY is 0.14. This is not a "sector exposure" buy; it must be underwritten as a **single-asset venture bet**, which caps size regardless of how attractive the mean is.
- **Kelly logic.** Scenario set ($84 / $150 / $321) is roughly symmetric with a modest upward skew and enormous dispersion. A half-Kelly allocation on a wide-dispersion, 50%-vol, negative-momentum, credibility-impaired name with an adverse 11-week catalyst is **1–2%**, not 4%.

Plus the decisive risk-management constraint the other agents surfaced: **an unknown here is binary and 11 weeks away** (Q4 print + 2027 guidance + HHT/obesity readouts all on Feb 11). Sizing as if that event has already resolved would be a process error.

**Build:** 1.0–2.0% band; **1.5% is the recommendation** for a diversified multi-strategy book. **Pass entirely** if (a) the portfolio is already >25% healthcare / >10% small-mid biotech, or (b) the mandate prohibits pre-revenue-catalyst single-asset concentration. **Downsize to 0.75%** if the fund already owns BBIO or Ionis (competitive overlap).

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector:** Adds to Healthcare/biotech. RNAi is a defensible sub-sector, but the Sector Researcher rates the *investable* class NEUTRAL precisely because multiples compress faster than revenue grows. Do not let a "cheap biotech" label justify breaching a sector cap.

**Factor exposures this ADDS (all unintended unless explicitly wanted):**
| Factor | Exposure added | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| **Duration / real-rate sensitivity** | **High — highest in peer set** | Macro is explicit: beta 0.27 is a *co-movement* measure and is misleading; this is a long-duration asset in a bear-steepening tape. Adds rate risk a low-beta label conceals |
| **Idiosyncratic / binary event risk** | **Very high (92% of variance)** | Concentrated, undiversifiable. Size accordingly |
| **Negative momentum** | High | −62% YTD; will drag any momentum/trend screen |
| **US drug-pricing policy beta** | High | MFN, IRA, 340B — a distinct, non-diversified policy factor |
| **Market beta** | **Low (~0.14–0.50)** | Genuine positive: diversifies an equity book |
| **Healthcare value/quality** | Moderate | GAAP profitable, positive FCF, net cash — rare in the peer set |

**Correlation:** at 0.27 vs XBI and 0.19 vs BBIO, ALNY is **not** substitutable for existing biotech exposure — treat it as a new, uncorrelated risk line. **Pair opportunity:** if the book owns BBIO (0.19 correlation, direct competitor), long-ALNY/short-BBIO is a legitimate way to isolate ATTR-CM share shift while neutralizing sector beta — arguably a better expression than a naked long.

**Bottom line:** the position is *additive to diversification* (low market/sector correlation) but *additive to concentration* (single-asset, single-policy factor). Both effects are why 1.5%–3% is right and 5% is not.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **SCALE IN — do not buy at once**

Current price $150.57 sits ~2% above the 52-week low ($147.82, 19 Nov) and ~82% below the median PT ($273.5). Tempting to back the truck up. Don't — the Feb 11 stack is the reason.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — Now** | **0.75%** | At market, $148–156 | Board Chair ($156.82) and director Sigal ($152.25) bought open-market Nov 9–10 — the most credible positive signal in the dataset; anchor near their prints |
| **2 — Now (structural)** | **0.75%** | Immediately, conditional | Only if tranche 1 fills; do not chase above $165 |
| **3 — Post-print** | **+1.0 to 1.5%** | After Feb 11, 2027 **only if**: Q4 AMVUTTRA ≥ $1.10B (no sequential decline) **and** 2027 TTR guide ≥ high-teens % | **This is where the Growth thesis earns its size** |
| **Alternative for event-risk mandates** | 0.75% equity + **Feb/Mar put spread** sized to position | Instead of tranche 3 | Two consecutive −25% earnings reactions justify defined-risk structure; Alt Data's "guidance + readout stack makes the tail two-sided" supports a spread, not a naked call |

**Explicit rule:** reduce to **1.0% before Feb 11** if the position has run above $200 into the print. Do not carry 3% through an unresolvable binary you have been warned about.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Price stop — $118 (−22%):** below which EV ≈ 2.4x 2027E sales and the market is pricing a hard franchise peak. *Caveat:* at 50% annualised vol this is a **review trigger, not a resting market order** — a 3σ week is normal here. Fundamental triggers dominate.

**Thesis invalidation — EXIT on any two of:**
1. **Q4'26 AMVUTTRA < $1.10B** (sequential decline) **AND** 2027 TTR guide below ~$4.5B → the "conversion lag, not demand destruction" thesis is dead.
2. **Product gross margin < 70% for two consecutive quarters** (Q3'26: 72.0% product GM, from ~87% in Q1'25). This breaks "platform leverage."
3. **Attruby captures >40% of new ATTR-CM starts** (BBIO is explicitly targeting 30–40%).
4. **OPDP untitled letters escalate** to a warning letter, or a DOJ/FCA inquiry into ATTR-CM promotion.
5. **ANDA/BPCIA notice letter filed against vutrisiran with a credible invalidity theory** (patent-eligible since 13-Jun-2026 — the "most underappreciated legal tail").
6. **Convert repayment stress:** 2027–28 converts (~$1.3B) cash-settled **while** revenue stalls → net cash flips to material net debt inside 24 months.
7. **Further senior commercial churn** or failure to backfill CCO by Q1'27.

**Trim triggers:**
- **$250–275 (median PT band):** trim ⅓ — the easy re-rating is captured.
- **$290–320 (near bull case / high-end PTs):** trim ½, and require the fundamentals to have caught up (two consecutive guidance-consistent quarters) to hold the remainder.
- **$350+ (bull case realized):** exit residual unless nucresiran Phase 3 has de-risked the 2030+ franchise.

**Positive re-rating signals to size up against:** MFN/TrumpRx agreement with explicit tariff exemption (Geo Legal: improves rating Low-Medium); formal dismissal/settlement of the class action; two clean quarters of AMVUTTRA re-acceleration; nucresiran Phase 3 positive (2027).

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — 1.5%, path to 3.0%**

**Not "Pass,"** because: net cash ($1.6–2.3B, unresolved between agents), positive FCF, $1B buyback, $0 goodwill, clean accounting, low market correlation, +82% to median PT, board members buying at 12-month lows, and a genuinely mispriced platform. The bear case is public and priced.

**Not "Buy full size,"** because: 92% idiosyncratic variance, 49.8% vol, a filed securities class action, a 33:1 insider sell ratio into two guidance cuts, a departing CCO, guidance credibility that has not yet been re-established, gross margin down ~1,500bp in six quarters, and an 11-week catalyst that the only leading-indicator agent reads as a **4–7% revenue miss**.

**This is a starter position with an option-like payoff, not a core holding.** Size it so a −44% bear case (Short Analyst's $84) costs ~65bp of the portfolio — painful, not disqualifying — while the +113% bull case ($321) contributes ~+170bp.

---

### Data gaps flagged for the memo
1. **Quant Analyst report is empty** — no systematic factor/screen input. The largest single gap.
2. **Value Researcher truncated mid-sentence** at the valuation section; no explicit verdict or P/B figure.
3. **Net cash disputed:** Fin Risk $1.63B (YE25) vs Value Researcher $2.3B (Q3'26). Fin Risk also flags **interest expense ($365M TTM) inconsistent with ~$1.28B of 0–1% converts (~28% implied cost)** — likely undisclosed royalty/Blackstone-style obligations. **This must be resolved from the debt footnote before sizing above 1.5%.** It is the one gap that could change the recommendation.
4. **Q3'26 cash balance unavailable** — all liquidity ratios are ~11 months stale.
5. **MFN/TrumpRx participation status unconfirmed** — a live binary for US net price.
6. **Beta is reported three ways** (0.27 profile / 0.50 vs XBI / 0.84 vs SPY). I used **0.50 vs XBI with R² 0.077**; size on the idiosyncratic variance, not the beta.
7. **ARWR/BBIO peer multiples unavailable**; ARWR revenue is milestone-lumpy and not comparable.

**Recommendation summary: INITIATE 1.5% (two 0.75% tranches at $148–156), cap 3.0%, add only after Feb 11, 2027 confirmation, price-review stop $118, exit on any two thesis-invalidation triggers.**

## SECTOR BRIEF — ALNY (Alnylam Pharmaceuticals) | Data as of 20 Nov 2026

### 1. Sector Overview

ALNY sits in **Biotechnology — oligonucleotide/RNAi therapeutics**, a sub-sector of the $1.97T-revenue (FY25, 22-company sample) US-listed Healthcare complex, whose aggregate gross margin is ~65% and net margin ~13.5%. The modality is no longer speculative: Alnylam alone has delivered **seven FDA-approved RNAi products in under nine years** (latest: Livsayis/cemdisiran, approved 19 Nov 2026 and commercialised by Regeneron), and the class is now contesting large cardiometabolic indications (ATTR-CM, hypertension, MASLD) rather than only ultra-rare orphan disease. That migration is the pivotal sector fact: it multiplies the TAM but simultaneously converts RNAi economics from **orphan pricing (high price, negligible competition)** to **cardiology pricing (payer scrutiny, oral and gene-editing rivals, share warfare)**. Sector structure is oligopolistic at the platform level (Alnylam, Ionis, Arrowhead, plus licensees Regeneron, Novartis, AstraZeneca, Roche) but brutally competitive at the asset level, where a single indication (ATTR-CM) now hosts Alnylam's Amvuttra, BridgeBio's Attruby, Pfizer's Vyndaqel/Vyndamax, and Ionis/AstraZeneca's eplontersen. Capital intensity is low (CMO-based manufacturing, 82% gross margins) and switching costs are moderate (chronic injectables with mortality benefit), while barriers to entry are high on IP/formulation chemistry but falling on clinical execution — a classic **"high barriers at the gate, crowded inside"** configuration.

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Platform optionality converts to royalty cash at zero commercial cost.** Livsayis (cemdisiran) approval gives ALNY milestones plus tiered royalties on a Regeneron-funded gMG launch; Regeneron's CIDEBsiRNA showed first-in-human liver-fat normalisation in MASLD (Nov 2026), and zilebesiran (hypertension, Roche-partnered) addresses a multi-tens-of-millions-patient pool. This is non-dilutive, high-margin revenue layered on existing R&D spend.
- **ATTR-CM class expansion + best-in-class durability data.** Five-year HELIOS-B data (AHA, Nov 2026) show sustained mortality/morbidity benefit for Amvuttra, supporting duration of therapy and share-of-voice versus oral stabilisers; ATTR-CM diagnosis rates are still structurally under-penetrated globally, so the pool is growing faster than the number of competitors.
- **Operating leverage is now visible in the P&L.** Operating margin went from **-83.9% (FY21) → -15.4% (FY23) → -7.9% (FY24) → +13.5% (FY25)** on 49.8% five-year revenue CAGR; Q3'26 operating income of $346M (23.7% margin) confirms the model scales without proportionate SG&A (SG&A flat at ~$322–348M/quarter since 2025).

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **ATTR-CM share loss is real and priced in brutally.** BridgeBio's Attruby is targeting 30–40% of the ATTR market and is "cruising toward blockbuster"; ALNY cut 2026 ATTR guidance on 29 Oct 2026, driving a **-25% one-day move** and a **-62% YTD share price** ($400 → $151). A second air-pocket occurred 30 Jul 2026 (-28% on the day, $287 → $205) — two guidance disappointments in one year destroys management credibility on the growth algorithm.
- **Growth deceleration and gross-margin erosion.** Revenue growth has collapsed from **+65.2% (FY25) to +16.8% YoY (Q3'26: $1,458M vs $1,249M)**, and gross margin fell to **75.2% in Q3'26 from 84.2% a year earlier** — royalty stacking to licensors (Ionis, Arbutus/Tekmira legacy, Dicerna/Novo) plus Amvuttra profit-share mechanics. Mix shift into cardiology caps pricing power versus the orphan franchise.
- **Regulatory, legal and policy overhang.** A Pomerantz investigation opened mid-Nov 2026 following the guidance cut (securities-litigation risk); the RNAi patent estate remains actively litigated (LNP/mRNA assertions against Pfizer and Moderna); and IRA drug-price negotiation eventually reaches high-revenue single-source drugs — a structural ceiling on the long-duration pricing that orphan economics used to guarantee.

### 4. Peer Comparison Table (latest reported fiscal year unless noted)

| Company | Model | Revenue | YoY growth | Gross margin | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ALNY** | RNAi platform (siRNA) | $3,714M (FY25) | **+65.2%** (Q3'26: +16.8%) | 81.8% (Q3'26: 75.2%) | 13.5% (Q3'26: 23.7%) |
| IONS | Antisense platform | $944M (FY25) | +33.9% | 98.3% | -40.5% |
| ARWR | RNAi platform | $451M (FY26 Sep) | -45.7%* | 99.6% | -156.9% |
| BBIO | ATTR-CM stabiliser | $502M (FY25) | +126.3% | 94.4% | -113.4% |
| BMRN | Rare disease enzymes | $3,212M (FY25) | +12.9% | 77.1% | 16.6% |
| SRPT | Gene therapy / DMD | $2,198M (FY25) | +15.6% | 59.9% | -29.9% |
| NBIX | Neuroscience | $2,861M (FY25) | +21.5% | 98.2% | 21.6% |
| VRTX | CF / rare disease | $12,001M (FY25) | +8.9% | 86.2% | 34.8% |
| **Biotech peer median (7)** | | | **+15.6%** | **94.4%** | **-29.9%** |
| *Healthcare aggregate (22 cos.)* | | $1,972,294M | — | 65.3% | ~13.5% net |

*\*ARWR revenue is collaboration/milestone-lumpy; growth rate not comparable to product revenue.*

ALNY ranks **#2 of 8 on growth and #1 by a wide margin on profitability versus the biotech peer set** (only BMRN, NBIX and VRTX are operating-margin positive, all at slower growth). Its gross margin trails the platform peers (81.8% vs 94–99%) purely because it books product COGS and royalties while IONS/ARWR recognise licence revenue at ~100% margin — an accounting artefact, not an economic disadvantage. Market-cap aggregation for the pure biotech peers was unavailable from the data feed; the mega-cap Healthcare list supplied by the screener is not a valid comp set and is excluded.
